title: pilot-onboarding-flow-and-success-sla-ops-kickoff
topics: access and network setup (VPC, SSO, KMS)
milestone cadence: kickoff, mid-point, exec readout
summary: Kickoff for a 6-week pilot to validate Nightingale's multi-tenant summarization pipeline on Redwood. Agreed success criteria: p95 < 450ms for 1-2k qps burst pattern, qualitative fidelity target on summary eval set, and cost target within 30% of current baseline. Access window and security controls discussed; next steps include security docs, test dataset upload, and a tenant sizing spreadsheet. Mid-point review and exec readout dates tentatively scheduled.
next_steps: Redwood to share SOC2 summary and architecture diagram (Maya) by 2026-10-30
Customer to provide sampled dataset + readout prompts (Ravi) by 2026-11-03
Set up VPC peering test account and credentials (Victor + Liam) target 2026-11-05
Schedule mid-point performance review (w/ exec) for 2026-11-16 (Sara)
Redwood to send initial pilot runbook and benchmark template (Liam) by 2026-10-31
action_items: Maya Chen: Share security pack (SOC2, encryption, data retention) — due 2026-10-30
Liam O'Connor: Deliver benchmark harness + sample load script — due 2026-10-31
Ravi Patel: Upload 10k sample records and canonical prompts to S3 share — due 2026-11-03
Victor Huang: Provide VPC peering details and test IAM role — due 2026-11-05
Isabel Torres: Send list of required compliance checks and auditors contact — due 2026-11-02
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: All right, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Liam, our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Ravi Patel: Hey Maya, Sara here too, Sara Kim, CTO — hi.
[00:13] Sara Kim: Hi all.
[00:16] Liam O'Connor: Hi, great to meet you — quick agenda: align on success criteria, get access plan locked, and timeline to exec readout.
[00:29] Diego Alvarez: Sounds good. We're primarily looking to validate summarization latency under our peak synthetic traffic and ensure fidelity is acceptable.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Perfect, can we start with the success criteria — what would make this pilot a clear yes for Nightingale?
[00:44] Ravi Patel: We want p95 end-to-end on summaries under 450ms for single-region traffic, and for cost we need to be within 30% of what we pay now for our current hosted pipeline. Also security — SOC2 or equivalent — has to be validated.
[00:59] Isabel Torres: And we need KMS integration for key management and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[01:07] Liam O'Connor: Noted. On latency we usually break it down: model decode latency, network/egress, and post-processing. For load profile, can you share expected qps, and the percent of long sequences?
[01:24] Ravi Patel: Baseline is 200 qps steady, with 1-2k burst for up to 2 minutes every hour. 70% of requests are short (<= 256 tokens), 30% are long (up to 1024 tokens).
[01:38] Maya Chen: That burst pattern is helpful; we typically recommend a dedicated burst capacity for that shape, or autoscale policy with warm pools.
[01:46] Diego Alvarez: How precise are your p95 numbers in your benchmarks? We've seen variance across models.
[01:52] Liam O'Connor: We run p95 across multiple runs — we also simulate KV cache warmup. Important to mirror your cache hit rate; otherwise latency will look worse. We'll include KV cache priming in the harness.
[02:04] Sara Kim: On fidelity, we'll provide a small eval set with human labels. We want summaries to hit at least 0.78 ROUGE-L or equivalent human pass rate on key facts.
[02:17] Liam O'Connor: Sounds reasonable. We'll run both automated metrics and a small blind human eval at midpoint.
[02:24] Maya Chen: Security/access — Victor, any constraints on how we connect for the pilot? VPC peering vs private link?
[02:32] Victor Huang: VPC peering preferred. We need to avoid public egress. Also need SAML SSO for Console access and limited RBAC for Redwood engineers.
[02:41] Isabel Torres: And double check data residency — some records are EU-only, so we'd like model routing policy to keep them in eu-west.
[02:49] Liam O'Connor: We can configure region pinning and routing policy. For KMS we support customer-managed keys; we'll provide integration steps in the security pack.
[03:00] Ravi Patel: Great. Timeline — what's a realistic cadence? We're thinking 6 weeks. Kickoff now, access in week 1, baseline runs week 2, mid-point review week 3-4, exec readout week 6.
[03:14] Maya Chen: That aligns with our typical pilot. We should plan a 2-week active benchmarking window to hit different load shapes. Mid-point we'd present early results plus any risk items.
[03:24] Diego Alvarez: Who will own the benchmark harness on our side vs Redwood?
[03:28] Liam O'Connor: Redwood will supply a harness and load script; you will run it in your test VPC to validate network characteristics. We can also run a mirrored hosted run if you want comparison numbers.
[03:39] Sara Kim: Is that mirrored run going to disclose cost numbers? We need per-token and per-request cost to compute forecasts.
[03:46] Maya Chen: We'll provide cost breakdown: tokens, grooming, per-call overheads — we'll anonymize tenant usage if we run it on a shared pool. For Dedicated runs we can also give an estimate for reserved capacity.
[03:58] Ravi Patel: On data handling, can Redwood guarantee no persistent storage of raw PII? We have PHI fields in some docs.
[04:07] Isabel Torres: This is a hard blocker for legal if raw PHI persists.
[04:10] Liam O'Connor: We support redaction and have options: mask at client side, or in-transit redaction rules. For the pilot we'll demonstrate a flow that never writes raw payloads to disk and uses envelope encryption via your KMS. We'll document retention windows in the pack.
[04:26] Maya Chen: Okay, let's capture those items as action items.
[04:29] [05:00] Speaker 1: Sorry, slight audio glitch — can you repeat the KMS bit?
[05:04] Liam O'Connor: Yes — customer-managed KMS, envelope encryption, HSM-backed optional. We'll outline steps for key grant and rotation.
[05:14] Diego Alvarez: For the mid-point performance check, can we run a long tail latency analysis and also an A/B against our current model?
[05:22] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely. We'll provide A/B harness and the same dataset so you're comparing apples-to-apples.
[05:30] Sara Kim: For exec readout, we want a single slide with pass/fail on latency, fidelity, cost delta, and a recommended next step (prod pilot, dedicated, or don't proceed).
[05:41] Maya Chen: We'll prepare that. Proposed dates: Mid-point on 2026-11-16 and exec readout on 2026-11-30 — does that work?
[05:49] Ravi Patel: That aligns with our calendar.
[05:52] Maya Chen: Great. Any other risk items?
[05:55] Isabel Torres: Auditability — we need immutable audit logs exported.
[05:59] Liam O'Connor: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM and provide tamper-evident logs. We'll include retention policy options.
[06:07] Victor Huang: Networking — what ports and egress endpoints will you need?
[06:11] Liam O'Connor: We'll send a minimal list: control plane endpoints for model uploads and telemetry, and inference endpoints via private IPs over the peered VPC.
[06:21] Diego Alvarez: On benchmarking metrics, can we include cost per 1k requests and cost per quality unit?
[06:27] Maya Chen: We can compute cost/token and translate to cost per request given the dataset. We'll output a spreadsheet so you can slice by workload.
[06:35] [06:45] Ravi Patel: Anything else on the roadmap?
[06:48] Maya Chen: Quick recap — actions and owners, security pack, dataset upload, VPC setup, and the benchmark harness. Mid-point and exec readout dates as agreed. We'll follow up with invites and the runbook.
[06:59] Sara Kim: Thanks everyone, pleased with alignment.
[07:02] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll send the notes and action items. Bye.
